prerequisites: Prior knowledge of mechanisms acquired in the compulsory course MECANISMOS.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the principles of theory of machines and mechanisms
Knowledge and capacities for the calculation, design and testing of machines
Applied knowledge of machine balancing and regulation systems

Ability to draft and develop projects in the field of mechanical engineering, for the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical installations, industrial installations and plants and manufacturing processes
Ability to direct activities subject to the engineering projects described in the previous section
Ability to carry out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks
Ability to interpret technical projects and reports
Ability to evaluate the effectiveness, feasibility and quality of implemented solutions
Demonstrate the ability to analyze and synthesize
Acquire the ability to effectively solve problems
Acquire skills related to the use of computer programs for calculation, data analysis and processing, within their field of application.
Possess the ability to make decisions
Ability to apply knowledge to practice
Acquire the capacity for autonomous learning and concern for knowledge and lifelong learning

syllabus_topics: VIBRATIONS IN MACHINES. BALANCING AND ALIGNMENT OF ROTORS
teaching_methods: Completion of individual and team projects
assessment_rules: To pass the subject, a minimum score of 40% is required in each part or activity, and a combined overall score greater than 50%. In all cases and calls, if any of the mentioned minimums are not met, the overall grade for the subject will be FAIL. For the second call, students must present themselves for any tests not passed in the first call, maintaining the minimum grade in all of them. The exceptional evaluation consists of final written exams and equivalent tests for continuous and practical evaluation, with the same weighting percentages.
